correctness.rationale: For equal cycle evaluations the half-difference of ±1 orientation cochains is a cocycle with zero integrals, hence an integer vertex gradient h. Every X-directed edge has drop 0 or 1; identical cycle signatures fix every oriented directed cycle in X and Y. Legal flexes never touch its cyclic vertices, giving the necessary common anchor. At a positive maximum potential the induced set has no incoming external arcs and no directed cycle (all cyclic vertices have normalized h=0), so it contains a global source that can be flexed to decrease h by one. The dual negative minimum yields a global sink that increases h by one. Iteration gives Y; per-vertex signed flip counts give matching ℓ1 lower bound, optimized by a median when no cycles, or anchored by their common level. No infinite inference is drawn from the 62,804 finite orientation-pair checks.

originality.rationale: Full mathematical implication comparison found the novelty at frozen vertices of arbitrary directed cycles, rather than the previously known acyclic/contracted c-orientation lattice. Kozlov explicitly asks for a complete augmentation of signature; the cycle-anchor potential gives an if-and-only-if answer and an explicit all-orientations exact distance. value.rationale: Kozlov explicitly poses the component-classification problem as Question 2 after exhibiting a failure of signature alone. The cycle-anchor potential supplies an all-graph complete new algebraic invariant, detects equal-signature disconnected orientations and computes exact shortest source/sink flip sequences without collapsing frozen cyclic components. This is a structural solution to a motivated topology problem, not merely tabulation or arbitrary parameter slicing.
